newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends lower as speculators liquidate.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends lower as speculators liquidate.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended lower and toward the bottom of the session's range Friday, dragged down by an afternoon round of speculative selling, market sources said.
Traders said disappointed longs began liquidating positions after an early rally failed to spark enough momentum to carry the benchmark March contract through $1,390 a tonne resistance.
"When nothing happened on the upside the longs decided to get out of their positions ahead of the weekend," one trader said.
But traders said the March contract appeared to find good support at $1,365-$1,363, just beneath the session low.

Most-active March cocoa ended $11 a tonne lower, at $1,368, after ranging between $1,389 and $1,366. Spot December, which entered notice period on Thursday, ended $2 weaker, at $1,328, while the back months finished down $14 to $18.
As of Thursday, December's open interest stood at 1,243 lots, down 765 lots from the previous session. March open interest rose by 883 lots to 42,975 lots.
A total of of 183 delivery notices were issued Friday, as well as 183 stoppers. A cumulative 599 delivery notices have been issued since Thursday.
On the charts, traders pegged near-term March support at $1,365, then $1,355. Resistance was seen at $1,390, with the $1,400 level providing a strong psychological upside target.
Volume was fairly light, at an estimated 5,929 lots.
